name: Remaliah
title: Father of King Pekah of Israel
summary: Remaliah is primarily known from the Bible as the father of Pekah, who became king over the Northern Kingdom of Israel. He is mentioned repeatedly in connection with the Syro-Ephraimite War, where his son Pekah allied himself with Rezin, king of Aram, against Judah. Remaliah himself had no prominent political or religious role, but his name was used to identify his son Pekah.

keyEvents.title: Pekah, Son of Remaliah, Becomes King over Israel
keyEvents.description: Pekah, the son of Remaliah, seized power in Israel by killing King Pekahiah and became king himself. He reigned for twenty years in Samaria.

keyEvents.title: The Syro-Ephraimite Threat against Judah
keyEvents.description: Pekah, the son of Remaliah, allied with King Rezin of Aram and marched up toward Jerusalem to attack King Ahaz of Judah. This created great fear in Judah.

keyEvents.title: Isaiah's Prophecy about the Son of Remaliah
keyEvents.description: The prophet Isaiah comforted King Ahaz and said that the plan of Rezin and the son of Remaliah would not succeed. God assured him that the threat would not stand.

keyEvents.title: The Sign of Immanuel in the Context of the Threat
keyEvents.description: In connection with the threat from the son of Remaliah and Rezin, God gave King Ahaz through Isaiah the famous Immanuel sign as a promise of God's presence and protection.

keyEvents.title: Isaiah's prophecy about the fall of the son of Remaliah
keyEvents.description: Isaiah prophesied that before the child Maher-Shalal-Hash-Baz could say 'father' and 'mother', the wealth of Damascus and the plunder from Samaria (the kingdom of the son of Remaliah) would be carried away.
